captions.text: Welcome to our discussion on consistent hashing in
distributed systems. This technique is crucial for scaling
data storage and minimizing data movement when nodes
change. Naive Majulo based sharding doesn't scale well.
When the number of nodes changes, a large
portion of the data needs to be re
sharded, leading to significant data movement and potential
service disruption Consistent hashing uses, a logical ring
to map keys and nodes Punction with a
uniform distribution is critical to ensure that each
node is responsible for approximately equal portions of
the key space. The consistent hashing algorithm provides
a deterministic lookup process. It works by hashing
the key and then searching the logical ring
in a clockwise direction until it finds the
node responsible for that key. This results in
an o log n lookup time when using
assorted list or binary search. Vert node v
nodes help with load balancing by allowing a
single physical node to be responsible for multiple
portions of the key space. This evens out
load variance and simplifies rebalancing when nodes are
added or removed. Replica placement is critical for
data durability and availability. Consistent hashing places replicas
in a clockwise direction. Node failures are handled
by redirecting requests to the next available node.
Consistent hashing, particularly useful in large dynamic clusters
with read heavy workloads. It minimizes data movement
during scaling and no changes making it suitable
for systems that require high availability and low
latency. Thank you for joining me on this
exploration of consistent hashing and distributed systems. This
technique is a powerful tool for building scalable

data.title: Hash Space and Logical Ring
data.body: The hash space is typically 2^32-1. Keys and nodes are mapped onto this space, and the node responsible for a key is the one closest to the key's hash value in a clockwise direction.
bullets: Keys and nodes are mapped onto the ring

scenes.title: Core Consistent Hashing Algorithm
scenes.narration: The Consistent Hashing algorithm provides a deterministic lookup process. It works by hashing the key and then searching the logical ring in a clockwise direction until it finds the node responsible for that key. This results in an O(log N) lookup time when using a sorted list or binary search.

data.title: Replica Placement and Failure Handling
data.body: Replicas are placed by moving R nodes clockwise from the primary node. This ensures data is durable and available even in the event of node failures.

scenes.title: When to Use Consistent Hashing
scenes.narration: Consistent Hashing is particularly useful in large, dynamic clusters with read-heavy workloads. It minimizes data movement during scaling and node changes, making it suitable for systems that require high availability and low latency.
